description: Annotations for the 29 example Tickets of the evidence report, keyed by ticket number. Each ticket names its A-N example; each example carries the condensed review note (the requester's first-person paraphrase, null where the report gives none) and its pattern's questions for Oliver. Shown on evidence only; no matching rule reads this file.

A.title: Romarian Alleyne: different jobs
A.summary: Separate morning/afternoon periods and different job identifiers. The job identifiers may distinguish these without any time parsing.
A.review_note: This does not show a company false positive. My concern was separate periods that otherwise look like the same job, so we need the real automated and human rules.
questions_for_oliver: Using B’s two visits to the same job, show how the current check distinguishes separate periods from repeated work. Does it use time, or does a person decide?
What is the intended unit of submission: one employee-day, one job or one period? How should split work be recorded while preserving job allocations?
A.what_the_answer_changes: Whether the fix is time parsing, a clearer daily form, or both.

B.title: Patrick Gittens: same job, separate visits
B.summary: Lears, job 20105, on 7 October; two one-hour periods. Both Approved with nonzero jobs, but not Keyed. This is closer to the original concern than A.
B.review_note: Both seem to have been accepted. Was that because someone checked the times? Also, what does Keyed False mean after approval?
questions_for_oliver: Using B’s two visits to the same job, show how the current check distinguishes separate periods from repeated work. Does it use time, or does a person decide?
What is the intended unit of submission: one employee-day, one job or one period? How should split work be recorded while preserving job allocations?
B.what_the_answer_changes: Whether the fix is time parsing, a clearer daily form, or both.

C.title: Peter Holder: priority example
C.summary: Same work on 28 September. Only the ticket number, ID and creation/modification/approval timestamps differ. Both are Approved and Keyed with job 41215.
C.review_note: This looks like the strongest example of an undetected duplicate, possibly paid twice. Keep it as the lead example, but ask Oliver whether it was handled somewhere we cannot see.
questions_for_oliver: Were these caught or missed? If caught, where is that decision recorded when both retain nonzero job numbers?
For Peter’s pair, show which ticket was retained and trace both through accounting and payment. Were both paid, or was one excluded elsewhere?
C.what_the_answer_changes: Whether the gap is detection, recording the review decision, or preventing a second payment.

G.title: Kerriann white: spacing in time

pattern.title: The same claim looks different as text

G.summary: Same job and work fields; time spacing differs. Both tickets are Pending and not Keyed.
G.review_note: Show Oliver this one explicitly. Why are there two submissions with slightly different spacing? Does the red warning merely alert someone, or does it record or block anything? I cannot tell whether Pending means waiting or already caught.
questions_for_oliver: Did the warning catch G and H despite the spacing differences, and were these tickets awaiting review or deliberately held?
What identifies the employee and work period in the actual check? Are names/times controlled fields, and does Modified By reveal a user edit, approval or automated update?
G.what_the_answer_changes: Whether to normalize inputs, fix employee identification, or record warning and review outcomes more clearly.

H.title: Mario Collymore: name variation

pattern.title: The same claim looks different as text

H.summary: Mario Collymore versus Mariocollymore for 23 September. Modified By is Tracy Whitehall versus Oliver Williams. The Pending ticket was created on 27 September, before the Approved/Keyed ticket on 29 September.
H.review_note: Why did the name change, and what do the two Modified By names mean? My tentative guess was that one ticket had not been reviewed, but it could be a replacement or a held duplicate. The spelling does not establish intent.
questions_for_oliver: Did the warning catch G and H despite the spacing differences, and were these tickets awaiting review or deliberately held?
What identifies the employee and work period in the actual check? Are names/times controlled fields, and does Modified By reveal a user edit, approval or automated update?
H.what_the_answer_changes: Whether to normalize inputs, fix employee identification, or record warning and review outcomes more clearly.

I.title: Damar Graham: occupation and site change

pattern.title: A new ticket may replace an earlier one

I.summary: An Approved/Job 0 record differs from the apparent original in occupation, site and description. Rejected row 999 connects the road-preparation and plainer wording.
I.review_note: Why do the occupation, site and work description vary so much if staff considered this the same claim? What does Rectro ticket mean, and which original did they identify?
questions_for_oliver: Using J, can an employee correct, cancel or resubmit to another supervisor, and can both reviewers see the earlier claim? Why did the time and supervisor change?
Using I, what evidence linked the records despite different occupation, site and description? Is the valid ticket explicitly linked to the superseded one?
I.what_the_answer_changes: Whether the main need is overlap detection or a correction workflow that leaves only one valid claim.

J.title: Orlando Richards: time and supervisor change

pattern.title: A new ticket may replace an earlier one

J.summary: Same job, overlapping periods and compatible descriptions; different supervisors. Both are Pending/not-Keyed, with Modified By Oliver Williams. The later ticket changes the start time.
J.review_note: These cannot be separate additive shifts as written. Is this a legitimate correction or another attempt to get an outstanding claim approved? I need the workflow and the time-comparison logic before judging intent.
questions_for_oliver: Using J, can an employee correct, cancel or resubmit to another supervisor, and can both reviewers see the earlier claim? Why did the time and supervisor change?
Using I, what evidence linked the records despite different occupation, site and description? Is the valid ticket explicitly linked to the superseded one?
J.what_the_answer_changes: Whether the main need is overlap detection or a correction workflow that leaves only one valid claim.

M.title: Weston Holder: both records marked Job 0

pattern.title: A payment component may be repeated

M.summary: Both carry Job Work Pay 50 and are Approved/Keyed with Job 0. The ticket containing hours was created on 15 September; the no-hours ticket followed on 21 September.
M.review_note: Could one be an incomplete claim and the other a correction? Why were both marked, and where is the valid claim? My original idea that hours were added later is contradicted by the creation dates.
questions_for_oliver: Why are both M records Job 0? Which ticket or accounting entry retained any valid payment, and could either claim have been wrongly excluded?
Do the two Job Work Pay amounts represent the same entitlement? How are those payments linked to labour claims or replacements?
M.what_the_answer_changes: Whether checks need to compare payment components and replacement links rather than reject whole tickets.

N.title: Toyna Elcock: retrospective task claims

pattern.title: The work date is buried in the description

N.summary: Both Date cells say 11 September and Job Work Pay is 20, but descriptions name the 9th and the 7th. Time and labour hours are zero.
N.review_note: This looks like catch-up invoicing for missed dates. How is it reviewed, and is any logic enforced? I wondered whether it needs manual handling; ask what information would allow a reliable check.
questions_for_oliver: What does Date represent here, and how are the actual service date and any earlier claim/payment checked?
Is the check currently manual because service dates are free text, or is there structured information elsewhere?
N.what_the_answer_changes: Whether to capture service dates explicitly and check claim history; free text alone does not make this inherently unautomatable.
